topicCandidates: A bounded profession-retrieval sweep for regulated or duty-ambiguous veterinary, mental-health, welfare, childcare, architecture, electrical, and laboratory roles.
Natural inline introduction of glossary terms already declared by existing articles, beginning with single-term mismatches.
Search routing to comparison guides where an ordinary job title cannot safely determine a residence status.
userSituations: A veterinarian or veterinary worker assumes that clinical work with animals belongs to Medical Services.
A psychologist, counselor, or social worker does not know whether the advertised title refers to a protected qualification, licensed act, or general support work.
A nursery, preschool, or childcare worker needs to separate teaching, childcare, welfare, and support duties.
An architect, architectural designer, electrician, or electrical engineer searches by an English title that can hide materially different professional, licensed, technical, or sector work.
A reader sees a Japanese term in an article's terminology section even though the prose never introduced it.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Professional licensing and immigration authorization are separate; satisfying one does not establish the other.
An English profession title can cover protected and unprotected activities, several workplaces, and different contracting structures.
Veterinary work must not be inferred to be Medical Services merely because it is clinical, while general animal care is not automatically the narrow Skilled Labor animal-training activity.
Electrician and electrical engineer are not interchangeable retrieval conclusions; technical design, installation, construction, maintenance, supervision, and licensing facts must be separated.
A metadata term should be introduced only when it assists the explanation; otherwise it should be removed rather than mechanically inserted.
jurisdictionVariables: The actual duties, time allocation, workplace, organization, contract, education, experience, remuneration, and work location.
The exact Japanese occupation or protected title, governing regulator, licence or registration, and scope of reserved activity.
The candidate residence status, sector or program rules, side activities, and any status-based work authorization.
Whether a declared glossary term is actually taught or used in the canonical article prose.

contentImpacts.reason: Route ambiguous profession searches to the general comparison method without assigning a status from a title.
Add a visible comparison boundary for veterinary, mental-health, welfare, and childcare roles.
Repair the first bounded set of single-term prose mismatches and preserve the remaining manual-review queue.

scopeBoundaries: Do not create a standalone guide for every profession or present a search alias as an immigration classification.
Do not imply that an overseas qualification automatically permits protected practice in Japan.
Do not map electrician to professional engineering, animal care to Skilled Labor, or a healthcare workplace to Medical Services without the controlling duties and rules.
Do not mechanically insert every metadata term; use or remove it according to the article's real teaching purpose.
Do not confer reviewed status through research or implementation.

scopeApproval.note: The editor approved the recommended profession-retrieval sweep and a bounded 16B-2 implementation rather than thin profession-specific articles.
